sharedArchitecture: src/mcp-server.js redirects non-JSON stdout writes to stderr and remaps console.* to stderr so MCP stdio stays machine-readable.
Most tools use src/index.js:createGeminiSession(), which delegates to src/browser.js:ensureBrowser() and src/gemini-ops.js:createOps(page).
src/browser.js auto-starts a detached daemon when needed, acquires a CDP endpoint, finds or opens a Gemini tab, and disconnect() leaves the browser alive under daemon TTL control.
Most handlers call disconnect() on controlled success/failure paths, but the code does not use finally blocks, so uncaught mid-handler failures can skip cooperative cleanup.

tools.name: gemini_generate_image

parameters.name: newSession
parameters.description: Start from a fresh chat before generating.

parameters.name: referenceImages
parameters.description: Local file paths uploaded before the prompt is sent.

parameters.name: fullSize
parameters.description: Download the full-size image instead of saving a preview extraction.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Wait budget in milliseconds for Gemini to finish generation.

outputs.success: Returns MCP text content announcing the saved local file path. In preview mode raw base64 is intentionally not returned; the handler writes a file under config.outputDir and returns only the path.
outputs.failure: Returns MCP text content with isError=true for login failure, upload failure, generation failure, or crash.

sideEffects: Auto-starts or reuses the daemon-backed browser session through createGeminiSession().
Performs a login precheck and aborts if Gemini is not logged in.
May switch the current model to Pro via ops.ensureModelPro().
Uploads each reference image from the local filesystem when referenceImages is non-empty.
Writes a local image file under config.outputDir on success.
When newSession=true, the current implementation clicks the new-chat button twice: once before reference upload and again immediately before generateImage().
Normal paths disconnect the CDP session after the tool finishes, leaving the browser alive under daemon TTL.

longRunningNotes.notes: Documented as a synchronous blocking tool. Handler text says typical runtime is 60-120 seconds and callers should budget at least 120000ms.

sharedEntrypointDependencies: src/index.js:createGeminiSession() is the common high-level entrypoint for building an ops/page/browser session.
src/browser.js:ensureBrowser() auto-starts the detached daemon if needed, acquires a CDP endpoint, and finds or opens a Gemini tab; disconnect() leaves the browser alive under daemon TTL.
src/gemini-ops.js:checkLogin(), ensureModelPro(), uploadImage(), and generateImage() provide the concrete automation used here.

migrationStatus.reason: Part of the current MCP surface and central to the product; no concrete source evidence justifies deferral or removal.

tools.name: gemini_browser_info

outputs.success: Returns MCP text content containing JSON for daemon URL/port/status, browser CDP port/wsEndpoint/pid/headless flag, and selected config values.
outputs.failure: Returns MCP text content with isError=true when the daemon is unreachable or unhealthy.

sideEffects: Does not call createGeminiSession(); instead it talks to the daemon HTTP endpoints directly.
Calls /health and then /browser/acquire, so the command is not a pure read: acquire can start or reuse the browser and will reset the daemon TTL.
Exposes daemon and browser connection details such as wsEndpoint and pid in the returned JSON payload.
Unlike the other handlers, this tool does not call disconnect() because it never creates a Puppeteer CDP session.

longRunningNotes.notes: Uses AbortSignal timeout guards (3s for /health, 5s for /browser/acquire) but is not documented as a long-running tool.

sharedEntrypointDependencies: src/index.js:createGeminiSession() is intentionally bypassed here; this is the one public MCP tool that does not build an ops/page/browser session.
src/browser.js still defines the daemon contract this tool depends on: the same localhost daemon URL, /health probe, and /browser/acquire semantics.
src/gemini-ops.js is not used by this tool; diagnostics come directly from config plus daemon HTTP responses.

migrationStatus.reason: Connection diagnostics are part of the current public interface and are especially important during a migration away from MCP transport.
